replies.author: Karfman
replies.body:
I think you misunderstood that. I don’t see myself as a ‘hater’ per se. I approach this pretty pragmatically. The points that keep getting brought up here are basically identical to what the blockchain community kept telling itself for years.

When it comes to AI in games, I see it in a more nuanced way. A good game can still succeed even if it visibly uses AI but it has to provide its own added value. Everything I’ve seen here so far feels like baby’s first steps, or like a four-year-old’s drawing you put on the fridge… nice for your immediate circle, sure, but not really suitable as a product.

There are a few exceptions, like some of the asset threads, which I personally find pretty shitty from a moral standpoint. It’s not sustainable, and it won’t improve my long-cherished hobby one bit. That said, I do understand the basic idea a lot of people are coming from. Creating something yourself is cool, and now there’s this toolbox that supposedly offers a lot of shortcuts.

Your animations, for example, are somewhat of an outlier compared to the usual slop. When I see something like ‘1492 colonization of the new world’ on Steam, I feel like throwing up. They literally just took old sprites and fed them into an AI… With the images I’ve seen from you, at least I don’t feel instantly put off.

As for your question, if there’s a demo on Steam, sure, I’d give it a try. Then I can assume it’s reasonably safe and won’t fry my setup. I’ll just quote another user from a different thread here to illustrate the issue:

‘I was making a similar visually styled game that was trying to set my PC on fire with 92°C temps after just 30 minutes of play…’

\--> I simply don’t have confidence in the fundamental skills needed to write reliable, safe software when I read things like that. If a game makes it onto Steam, I assume it’s at least basically okay.
